description: Composite characterization figure of seven panels of four different kinds. (a) is an XRD plot of intensity (a.u.) versus 2θ (degree), scanned from 40 to 120, with two stacked patterns — black "Cast Specimen" and red "Hot forged specimen" — whose reflections are indexed α110, γ111, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311 and γ222; the legend states "α:ferrite (δ/α), γ:austenite". (b) and (c) are optical micrographs of the cast specimen showing plate/dendritic second phase (blue arrows) in a lighter matrix. (d) and (e) are optical micrographs of the hot forged specimen in which the second phase is elongated and aligned, with a remnant dendritic feature arrowed in (e). The layout order of the supplied panels is (a),(b),(c),(d),(f),(e),(g). (f) is an SEM image of the hot forged specimen labelling elongated γ within the δ matrix, 10 µm scale bar. (g) is an EBSD phase map superimposed on the image-quality map, 200 µm scale bar, legend red = BCC, green = FCC. Together the panels argue that a δ-ferrite + austenite dual-phase structure exists in both the cast and the hot forged condition, and that forging only partially dissolves the cast dendritic austenite.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an XRD plot with 2θ (degree) on the abscissa from 40 to 120 and Intensity (a.u.) on the ordinate, containing two stacked patterns labelled 'Cast Specimen' (black) and 'Hot forged specimen' (red).
The XRD patterns in (a) are indexed with austenite reflections γ111, γ200, γ220, γ311, γ222 and ferrite reflections α110, α200, α211, and the in-panel legend reads 'α:ferrite (δ/α), γ:austenite'.

Panels (b) and (c) are optical images of the cast specimen and (d) and (e) are optical images of the hot forged specimen, (f) is an SEM image of the hot forged specimen, and (g) is an EBSD phase map superimposed on the image-quality map, with δ = delta ferrite and γ = austenite.
Blue arrows in panels (b), (c) and (e) mark the dendritic-type austenite features visible in the micrographs.
Panels (d) and (e) show an aligned, elongated second-phase morphology consistent with the working direction of hot forging, in contrast with the coarser plate/dendritic morphology of (b) and (c).
Panel (f) carries a printed 10 µm scale bar, and the elongated phase is labelled γ within the δ matrix.
Panel (g) has a printed 200 µm scale bar and a legend in which red corresponds to BCC and green to FCC, with green elongated islands dispersed in a red matrix.
The caption and citing text state that ferrite was initially assumed to be δ-ferrite based on a Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase fraction plot (Fig. 1b).
The citing text states that the optical images in Fig. 2(b-e) confirm a dual-phase microstructure in both the cast and the hot forged specimens.

The citing text states that the austenite in the cast specimen has a dendritic structure and that some dendritic structure is still visible in the hot forged specimen (blue arrow in Fig. 2e), possibly due to insufficient soaking and dissolution before hot forging.

The citing text states that Rietveld refinement of the XRD data gives ~26 vol.% austenite in the cast sample and ~29 vol.% in the forged sample, i.e. the forged sample contains ~3% more austenite; these numbers are not printed in any panel of the figure.

The ferrite α110, α200 and α211 reflections and the austenite γ111, γ200, γ220, γ311, γ222 reflections appear in the same positions in the black cast and red hot forged patterns, indicating the same phases in both conditions.
